evaluation.positioning_hook: A timid logistics clerk at a supernatural death agency is forced into a field team of misfit monsters and weapons-grade weirdos, then discovers his erased-outburst power can end a British zombie threat.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise has a clean genre promise — office drudge becomes accidental weapon — and the creature-comedy energy is easy to sell. The appeal is more cult-forward than four-quadrant, though, because the slangy dialogue, dense mythos, and very specific comic register narrow the lane.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early: Francis wakes in the logistics division, gets tagged as a SINON, and is shoved onto a kill mission before he understands his own power. The mission engine is clear, though the terminology and world-specific jargon ask the audience to catch up quickly.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Francis has a usable contradiction — anxious pencil pusher versus latent cosmic force — and the team around him gives him contrast. The supporting players are vivid in voice, but most of them function primarily as comic pressure around Francis rather than carrying separate emotional arcs.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits to a strange, specific comic universe: death-toll spreadsheets, retro-futurist office tech, and a team of outlandish operators with distinct speech patterns. The boldness is strongest in the tonal mash of bureaucratic mundanity and supernatural combat, even if the underlying mission shape is familiar.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The script moves quickly from office introduction to team assembly to London combat, and the escalating pressure on Francis's wrist meter gives the action a readable engine. The central fight is propulsive and the reveal of his power lands as a payoff rather than a detour.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The idea of a death-division office worker whose outbursts are literally measured and weaponized feels fresh and immediately legible. The British zombie target and the team’s comic identities are memorable, though the broader mission structure still sits in recognizable monster-hunt territory.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: Comirum feels like a place with rules, hierarchy, and internal culture: the death board, the wrist meter, the field-unit hierarchy, and the office banter all imply a larger system. The world is story-generating and specific, even though this excerpt keeps most of the larger mythology just offscreen.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The voice is unmistakable: profanity, deadpan office comedy, creature-feature violence, and exaggerated character entrances all coexist in a very controlled register. The script knows exactly how silly, gross, and sincere it wants to be, which gives it a strong identity on the page.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are seeds of more beneath the surface — Francis's erased memory, the meaning of SINON, and Doreen's guarded authority — that suggest a larger mythology. In this excerpt, though, the emphasis stays on immediate comic action, so the deeper emotional reservoir is present more as promise than as fully dramatized subtext.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The team dynamic is lively: Francis/Ploy, Francis/Hal, Clara/Toast, and Doreen versus everyone all generate distinct comic friction. The ensemble has enough personality contrast that multiple pairings could carry scenes, which is a real asset for a feature built around a squad.

casting_characteristics: Ensemble of distinct adult character types
Francis requires a physically slight, anxious lead with strong comedic timing
Toast is a robot role with voice/performance capture potential
Clara, Hal, and Ploy each require highly specific comic rhythm

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Mostly interior with one major exterior action sequence

technical.vfx_details: Multicolor energy bursts, Francis's eye/forehead effects, the British zombie's regeneration, Toast's robotic body, and the opening surreal flash imagery all require digital augmentation.
technical.sfx_needs: Weapon transformations, body hits, limb loss, regeneration gags, and practical blood effects.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming or premium cable genre-comedy lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model; best suited to festival-to-platform or genre-streaming launch

cost.note: Contained interiors keep the footprint manageable, but the London night battle, creature work, and digital power effects push it above micro-budget.

cast.note: The ensemble is compact, but the script depends on a very specific comic chemistry across Francis, Doreen, Hal, Clara, Ploy, Jerry, and Toast.

location.note: Most of the story is contained, but the London exterior sequence, rooftop work, and night coverage add logistical complexity.

content.note: Frequent profanity, violence, blood, dismemberment, and zombie combat place it firmly in mature-content territory.

rights.note: No named real people, brands, music, or licensed IP are referenced in the excerpt.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The office world is the joke and the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The death-toll spreadsheets, cubicle bureaucracy, and wrist-meter surveillance give the concept a commercial hook that is instantly legible and easy to market. Buyers who want a genre piece with a workplace-comedy spine will see a lane for audiences who like their supernatural action filtered through office absurdity.
strengths.evidence: Francis asleep at his desk in Logistics Division, the green board reading 'Death toll for the week! Double check it!', and Doreen issuing the wrist device that measures outbursts.

strengths.what_it_means: The lead role gives an actor a playable arc from anxious underachiever to accidental powerhouse, which is the kind of transformation that can carry a feature and anchor a franchise if expanded. Mid-career comedic leads and actors looking to pivot into action-comedy would chase this because it lets them play panic, embarrassment, and release in one part.
strengths.evidence: He insists he is 'not a field guy,' spends the mission trying to avoid responsibility, then finally unleashes the multicolor beam that erases the zombie.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The team is a ready-made comic ensemble.
strengths.what_it_means: Hal, Clara, Ploy, Toast, and Doreen each have a distinct comic register, which gives the project multiple trailer moments and makes the ensemble feel castable rather than generic. Ensemble players, scene-stealing character actors, and directors who like banter-driven group chemistry will respond to how each member pops in a different way.
strengths.evidence: Hal's macho bragging, Clara's coked-up flirtation, Ploy's bass-heavy swagger, Toast's deadpan robotic contempt, and Doreen's no-nonsense command.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The tonal blend is highly ownable.
strengths.what_it_means: The script can sell as a supernatural action-comedy with a very specific voice, which helps it stand out in a crowded genre field. Buyers looking for something that can play to genre fans without feeling generic will notice the mix of profanity, bureaucracy, and creature violence.
strengths.evidence: The script jumps from a comic-sans death board to donut banter to a rooftop zombie fight without losing its voice.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The power reveal has a clean payoff shape.
strengths.what_it_means: Francis's ability is introduced as mystery, pressure, and embarrassment before it becomes spectacle, which gives the climax a satisfying reveal structure. That kind of delayed-payoff mechanic is attractive to producers because it creates a trailerable midpoint-to-finale escalation.
strengths.evidence: The wrist percentage climbs as Francis eats the hot dog, flashes back to the opening field image, and finally fires the 'Bang' beam.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The world suggests a larger mythology.
strengths.what_it_means: Comirum, SINONs, the outburst meter, and the erased-memory opening imply a bigger universe that could support sequels or spin-off thinking if the feature connects. Genre buyers and franchise-minded producers will see room for expansion beyond this one mission.
strengths.evidence: Doreen's line that Francis will be erased if he doesn't prove useful, plus the unexplained opening image of the ruined college and the missing people.

whats_special.headline: This script has a very marketable core: a deadpan office worker in a supernatural death bureau gets dragged into a monster-killing squad and discovers his panic is the weapon. The voice is specific, the ensemble pops, and the world feels like it could support more than one story if the feature lands.

lead_characters.name: Francis Booker
lead_characters.hook: Francis is a terrified logistics clerk who would rather hide behind spreadsheets than step into a fight, but his body keeps betraying him with strange, escalating power. He reads as a chronic underachiever with a sharp mouth, a blush-prone crush response, and a buried force that turns embarrassment into spectacle.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Jesse Eisenberg in The Social Network — a fast-talking, self-protective lead whose internal panic is the performance. Actors who can play brittle comedy and then flip into sudden authority will chase this because the role gives them a full transformation without losing the awkwardness that makes him human.

lead_characters.name: Doreen
lead_characters.hook: Doreen is the hard-edged supervisor who runs the room with clipped commands, dry contempt, and a buried sense that she has seen too much to indulge anyone's panic. She is all control on the surface, but the way she keeps Francis in play suggests a manager who knows exactly how expendable everyone is and still chooses to move them like pieces.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of command-center role Frances McDormand has in Fargo — a character whose authority is the drama and whose deadpan becomes the joke. Veteran actresses who can play steel, wit, and moral ambiguity in the same breath will want this because it lets them dominate scenes without needing action-showy material.

lead_characters.name: Hal
lead_characters.hook: Hal is the swaggering bruiser who treats danger like a stage and humiliation like foreplay, turning every room into a contest he expects to win. He is loud, performative, and weirdly lovable, with enough ego to be annoying and enough charm to make the team keep him around.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase lane of John C. Reilly in Walk Hard or Michael Shannon when he lets menace and absurdity share the frame — a big personality role that can steal scenes through commitment. Character actors with physical presence and comic timing will chase it because it gives them a chance to be both the punchline and the threat.

lead_characters.name: Ploy
lead_characters.hook: Ploy is a bass-blasting, fearless field fighter who talks like she is already halfway through the joke and halfway through the battle. She has the energy of someone who lives at full volume, but the script also gives her a real emotional function as the first person to tell Francis he has more in him than he admits.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of breakout sidekick-to-co-lead territory that made Lupita Nyong'o in Us so magnetic — physical confidence, comic timing, and a hidden emotional center. Actors who can bring charisma, rhythm, and action-readiness will want it because the part gets to be cool, funny, and essential to the climax.

lead_characters.name: Clara
lead_characters.hook: Clara is a coke-fueled flirt with a knife in her hand and zero interest in behaving like anyone's idea of a professional. She is reckless, horny, funny, and dangerous, the kind of character who can turn a room into chaos and still feel like the most alive person in it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of feral comic volatility Jennifer Coolidge can turn into gold — a role where the joke is the confidence and the confidence is the weapon. Actors who like playing high-wire comic chaos with a little menace will chase it because Clara gets to be outrageous without ever becoming generic.

lead_characters.name: Toast
lead_characters.hook: Toast is a sentient robot with a dry, contemptuous worldview and the patience of a machine that has already calculated everyone else's stupidity. He is the team’s deadpan skeptic, but the script keeps giving him action utility, which makes him feel like more than a punchline.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Alan Tudyk's performance work in Rogue One or K-2SO — voice-driven deadpan that still carries personality and timing. Performers who can do precision comedy through voice and movement will want it because the role lets them build a memorable character without conventional human behavior.

lead_characters.name: Jerry
lead_characters.hook: Jerry is the hungry, friendly office creature who feels like the most normal monster in the building. He is mostly a comic texture player here, but his easy rapport with Francis gives the world a lived-in, offhand strangeness.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of scene-stealing creature role that character actors and performance-capture performers enjoy because it can be played with physical specificity and comic warmth. It offers the same appeal as the more playful supporting creatures in Guardians of the Galaxy: a small part that can still become audience-favorite material.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to stage action-comedy with a sharp comic voice and a weirdly bureaucratic universe.
director_appeal.fit_profile: Second- or third-feature directors, or TV genre directors moving into features, who already know how to balance ensemble banter with clean action geography. This material rewards filmmakers who like performance-forward world-building, practical creature energy, and a tone that can pivot from deadpan office comedy to full-contact supernatural mayhem.
director_appeal.detail: The script gives a director a chance to make the world feel specific without needing a giant mythology dump, and the London fight offers a clear set-piece to show control of escalation. It will attract directors who want a project that is visually playful, actor-friendly, and built around rhythm rather than spectacle for spectacle's sake.

buyer_appeal.lane: Streaming genre-comedy / premium cable action-fantasy lane
buyer_appeal.detail: The cast can be built around one breakout lead and a handful of scene-stealing supporting players, so a buyer does not need a marquee ensemble to make the package work. The contained office setup plus one major night exterior gives it a manageable footprint, and the supernatural-comedy lane has a clear home on streamers that buy elevated genre with a strong voice.

considerations.area: The opening image is a mystery before the premise.
considerations.detail: The ruined-college flash and the silent, bloodied Francis are striking, but the script then resets into office comedy before the audience knows what the opening means. One lever would be to let that image echo a little sooner in the first act so the mystery feels like an active engine rather than a separate prologue.

considerations.area: Francis's power reveal could be seeded earlier.
considerations.detail: The hot dog trigger and the wrist meter give the climax a fun payoff, and the script already knows how to build toward it. A next pass could plant one more concrete clue in the office or briefing-room material so the final beam feels inevitable from the start.

considerations.area: The ensemble is strongest when it plays off Francis.
considerations.detail: The team members all have distinct voices, and the banter is lively, but most of their scenes orbit the same mission beat. The version of the script where one or two of them get a sharper personal objective in the first half would deepen the ensemble engine without changing the premise.

considerations.area: The London set-piece defines the budget lane.
considerations.detail: The rooftop chase, regeneration effects, limb-loss gags, and multicolor energy blast put this above a bare-bones indie footprint. The cleanest production path is to protect the contained office world and keep the exterior action concentrated into one major sequence, which preserves the movie's scale while keeping the shoot focused.

considerations.area: Toast and the zombie need clear technical planning.
considerations.detail: The robot performance and the regenerating British creature both depend on effects work that will need to be designed early. A practical-first approach with selective digital augmentation would protect the comedy timing and keep the action readable.
